newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins rise,ignore rest emerging debt dip.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins rise,ignore rest emerging debt dip.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds rose on Tuesday due to active client buying on news about forthcoming Russia sovereign and regional Eurobonds, ignored before on fears of U.S. interest rate hike, dealers said.
"MinFins are strong on client buying despite a decline on the rest of emerging markets, which are tracking U.S. Treasuries," a London bank dealer said.
"Last month there has been so much good news (about Eurobond issues) from Russia which were ignored because of negative news elsewhere," he added.
Brady market dealers said earlier the imminent Moscow Eurobond could be background for support. The roadshow for the City of Moscow's three-year $400 million Eurobond is due on May 11 to 23.
Like other emerging debt, MinFins are sensitive to any news which would suggest a further rise in U.S. interest rates, as this would push down U.S. Treasury bond prices.
On May 20 the U.S. policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee meets and could raise U.S. interest rates.
Dealers said the shortest tranche gained the most today, followed by other papers.
An ICFI Moscow Partners bank dealer said buying activity could be also higher ahead of annual coupon payment on May 14.

"One cannot say that U.S. inflationary fears are gone but buying is active, especially ahead of coupon payment. Anyway, we are not seeing big rises or big falls this week, some range-trading is likely," he said.
